g.text: Changes in an exposed rock outcrop (cross-sections, not to scale)
Part of the outer sheet has fallen
By day the outer sheet warms and expands more than the interior
(1); at night it cools and contracts (2).
These repeated stresses help cracks grow parallel to the surface,
between the sheet and the interior (3).
Part of the outer sheet detaches and falls (4): the outcrop peels
Heating and cooling is one contributing mechanism. Unloading and
other stress changes can also open surface-parallel cracks.
